newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao charged in vote-buying case.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao charged in vote-buying case.

text.p: Federal police indicted former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao on Wednesday in a three-year-old vote-buying case, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

The news agency said the Central Bureau of Investigation charged Rao and six others with allegedly paying legislators from a regional party to vote against a 1993 no-confidence motion which Rao's Congress party narrowly won.
Officials from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) later confirmed that Rao had been charged in the vote-buying case.
Earlier this year the CBI filed a case accusing Rao and other Congress leaders of bribing the regional lawmakers to win their votes. Rao and the Congress leaders have denied any wrongdoing.
The charges were filed on the same day that Rao appeared in a trial court in a separate criminal forgery case.

The former prime minister, who resigned in May after his Congress party lost general elections, has been named but not charged in a third case involving alleged criminal conspiracy to cheat. A hearing in that case was set for November 6.
